description: The bar chart illustrates the correlation values across three domains—Movies, Songs, and Basketball—for four distinct metrics: PopGT, PopGe, RPopGT, and RPopGe, as referenced in the paper “How Knowledge Popularity Influences and Enhances LLM Knowledge Boundary Perception.” The vertical axis represents “Correlation,” scaled from 0 to 0.7 in increments of 0.1, while the horizontal axis categorizes the domains. Each domain contains four bars, color- and pattern-coded according to the legend: solid orange for PopGT, orange with diagonal stripes for PopGe, solid blue for RPopGT, and blue with diagonal stripes for RPopGe. In the “Movies” category, PopGT is approximately 0.25, PopGe is ~0.1, RPopGT is ~0.35, and RPopGe is ~0.63. In “Songs,” PopGT is ~0.3, PopGe is ~0.08, RPopGT is ~0.5, and RPopGe is ~0.7. In “Basketball,” PopGT is ~0.06, PopGe is ~0.08, RPopGT is ~0.13, and RPopGe is ~0.22. The bars are grouped by domain and ordered consistently across categories, with RPopGe consistently showing the highest correlation in each group, and PopGe generally the lowest. The chart visually emphasizes the relative strength of correlation for each metric within each domain, suggesting that RPopGe (revised popularity based on ground truth and generated knowledge) tends to have the strongest correlation across all domains, particularly in Songs.
